scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance is primarily associated with the worship of the deity Ayyanar and is centered in the Thanjavur region.
Recent research has challenged the long-held belief that the dance originated from Maratha traditions.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: It is performed during religious festivals to honor Ayyanar and is also featured as a cultural performance during national events like Republic Day in New Delhi.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers fit inside a dummy horse frame made of lightweight materials.
They attach wooden legs to their feet to create a rhythmic tapping sound.
Performers often carry a sword or whip and may perform acrobatic movements.
on_screen: Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Typically performed by a pair of dancers.
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The dance is accompanied by a variety of instruments including the clarinet, drum, Kundalam, Naiyaandi Melam, Thavil, Nadhaswaram, Pambai, and Thalam.
Listen for the clarinet, drum, Kundalam, Naiyaandi Melam.
The music relies on a combination of wind and percussion instruments typical of Tamil Nadu folk traditions, designed to accompany the rhythmic tapping of the dancer's wooden hooves.
